# Firmware symbol families (E-M10 Mark I, body fw 1.4)

Machine-listed symbols for routines that the firmware repeats many times: per-class copies of the same
small routine, compiler entry stubs, and one-line field writers. Each family was found by an exact byte
match or byte-pattern scan over block 0 and is described once at the top of its section; the rows only
give the address, name and the parameter that differs. Hand-analysed symbols live in
[`symbol-map.md`](symbol-map.md); names guessed from log strings are in
[`symbol-strings.md`](symbol-strings.md). `tools/symbol_index.py` indexes all three.

Runtime base `0x7d991020`; addresses are runtime addresses.

## OlyHfwOpe sub-component table getters (pattern family)
Every function in block 0 with the exact byte sequence of `olyhfw_ope_subcomp_get45` `0x7e29cf9d`
(`mov d0,d1; exthu d1; cmp N,d1; bcc; exthu d0; asl2 d0; add OFF,a0; mov (d0,a0),a0; …; retf`) is a
bounds-checked getter over a pointer table inside a GUI screen object: `(a0=this, d0=u16 idx)` →
`idx < N ? *(this + OFF + idx*4) : NULL`. A byte-pattern scan on 2026-11-12 found **197** such functions
(OFF = 792 in 192 of them), all in banks `0x7e27`–`0x7e2c`; each GUI screen class has its own copy sized to
its number of sub-components. The ones already listed in the main table keep their earlier names; the
remaining 127 are listed here, named `olyhfw_subcomp_get<N>_<address>`. The xref column is Ghidra's
reference count (`—` where the function list has no entry).

## Cmp component Idle-enter copies (pattern family)
Every Cmp component class carries its own copy of the same "enter Idle" routine: a `call`+`ret` wrapper
followed by a body that sets the state word to 49 at `+948` and `+256`, `+636 = 466`, `+632 = 0` and logs
`"Cmp_Play%s Idle"` ([[cmp-component-framework]]). A byte-pattern scan on 2026-11-12 finds **28** copies in
banks `0x7e15`–`0x7e1c`; 19 wrappers were already labelled individually in the main table. The remaining 9
wrappers are listed here as `cmp_enter_idle_<address>`; each body sits 8 bytes after its wrapper.

## Replicated small routines (pattern families)
Groups of byte-identical or same-shaped routines that every component or GUI class carries its own copy
of. Found on 2026-11-12 by grouping block-0 functions with identical bytes and by byte-pattern scans;
rows already in the main table keep their earlier names. Names are `<family>_<address>`.

| family | copies | newly listed here |
|---|---|---|
| `guiobj_vstub_ret_m1` | 255 | 255 |
| `obj_clear_f24` | 45 | 45 |
| `obj_clear_f252_f256` | 35 | 35 |
| `cmp_release_f560` | 31 | 31 |
| `cb_f4_call_u16` | 29 | 29 |
| `cb_f36_call` | 29 | 29 |
| `cmp_state_enter_<N>` | 723 | 723 |

`cmp_state_enter_<N>`: `mov N,d0; mov d0,(948,a0); call body; ret` — the per-state wrappers of the Cmp
component state machine ([[cmp-component-framework]]); `+948` is the state word (49 = Idle, see the Idle-enter
family). State numbers seen and how many components carry each: 11×28, 13×28, 16×28, 18×28, 20×28, 22×28, 24×28, 26×28, 28×28, 30×28, 32×28, 34×28, 36×28, 38×28, 40×28, 42×28, 44×28, 46×28, 50×23, 52×20, 53×1, 54×18, 55×2, 56×15, 57×1, 58×16, 59×1, 60×13, 61×4, 62×11, 63×3, 64×10, 65×4, 66×9, 67×2, 68×9, 69×3, 70×9, 71×2, 72×9, 73×1, 74×6, 75×4, 76×4, 77×2, 78×4, 79×2, 80×3, 81×1, 82×3, 84×2, 86×1, 88×1.

## Entry stubs and one-line field writers (pattern families)
Listed 2026-11-12 from block-0 function entries whose bytes match exactly:
- **`entry_thunk_<addr>`** (2102): `call <addr+8>,[regs],N; ret` — an 8-byte stub that calls the body placed
  directly after it. The compiler emits these in front of bodies that save registers; the real work is in the
  body, so a stub's name says only where its body is.
- **`obj_clear_f<off>_<addr>`** (894): `clr d0; mov d0,(off,a0); retf` — zero one 32-bit field. In the Cmp
  component classes these clear the per-state slots `+952`…`+1020` that follow the state word `+948`.
- **`obj_set1_f<off>_<addr>`** (41): `mov 1,d0; mov d0,(off,a0); retf` — set one field to 1.

## Shared-body entry stubs (pattern family)
8-byte functions `call X,[regs],N; ret` whose target `X` is **not** the code right after them: a second
entry point into an existing body, with its own register-save mask. Many are Cmp component state helpers
that share one body per class. 1299 listed, named `entry_stub_<address>`; the role column gives the body.

## One-instruction accessors, empty functions and thunks
Functions whose whole body is one instruction plus return, classified from their disassembly on 2026-11-12.
The name says what the instruction does; the trailing address keeps names unique.
- `get_[u16_|u8_]f<off>_<addr>` / `set_[u16_|u8_]f<off>_<addr>`: read or write one field of the object in `a0`.
- `global_[u16_|u8_]<address>_get|set_<addr>`: read or write one global variable.
- `ret_ptr_<value>_<addr>`: return a fixed address (a static object or table) in `a0`.
- `nop_<addr>`: empty function (`retf`), typically a virtual method a class leaves empty.
- `thunk_to_<target>_<addr>`: `call target; ret`.

Counts: set 977, global 720, get 542, nop 405, thunk 308, ret 146. Total 3098.

## Two-instruction helpers
Bodies of exactly two instructions plus return, classified from their disassembly on 2026-11-12:
- `store[_u16|_u8]_<value>_f<off>|g<address>_<addr>`: store a constant into a field (`f`) or a global (`g`).
  Some `g` addresses are hardware registers (e.g. `0x9b20xxxx`); the name only records the store.
- `get_<s16|u16|s8|u8>_f<off>|g<address>_<addr>`: read a field or global and sign- or zero-extend it.
- `thunk_<s16|u16|s8|u8>_<target>_<addr>`: call `target` and narrow its result.
- `thunk_arg<s16|u16|s8|u8>_<target>_<addr>`: narrow the argument, then call `target`.
- `call0_<target>_<addr>`: call `target`, return 0. `call_arg0_<target>_<addr>`: call `target` with `d0 = 0`.

Counts: thunk 221, store 211, call0 40, get 38, call 35. Total 545.

## Vtable members (Ghidra class pass)
Functions that `tools/ghidra/VTables.java` and `ClassGraph.java` placed in a class: `<class>__vfn<N>_<addr>` is
slot N of that class's vtable, `<class>__ctordtor_<addr>` is a function that installs the vtable (a constructor
or destructor). `<class>` is the class name where a debug string gave one (e.g. `OlyHfwOpeSndCtlSoundEvFw`) and
`cls_<vtable address>` otherwise. A function shared by several classes is listed under the first class the
pass assigned it to. 4808 listed across 248 classes; 4 in the flash-write and firmware-update ranges are left out; 161 that already have a log-string name in `symbol-strings.md` are listed only there.

## Byte-identical routine copies (pattern family)
Unlabelled functions of 8 to 300 bytes whose bytes are exactly the same as at least three others
(`tools/func_patterns.py clusters 4 300`). Calls and branches are position-relative on this CPU, so
identical bytes at different addresses call *different* targets at the same distance: these are the same
source routine compiled once per class or per driver instance, each copy working with its own
neighbours. 716 functions in 91 groups. 367 of them (the 25 groups that were read) have a descriptive
name; the rest are named `copy<N>x_<first address>_<address>` so the copies can at least be recognised
as one routine, with the opening instructions quoted.

## Small call wrappers and forwarders (pattern family)
Unlabelled functions of at most 16 bytes whose body is one or two calls plus at most two set-up
instructions, classified from their disassembly on 2026-11-13 by `tools/func_patterns.py small 16`
(a leading stack-frame adjustment is ignored). 3407 listed. The name records the shape and the call target;
what the target does is described at the target, if it is labelled.
Where the call target already has a name in these documents, the row ends with `Target: <name>`.
The `call_<target>_ret_null` shape is this firmware's destructor convention: the labelled targets are
base-class destructors or teardown routines (`base_reset_vtbl_7e42c02c` ×608, `evtsrc_dtor` ×173,
`gui_view_dtor` ×54), and the wrapper is the derived class's destructor that has nothing of its own to
free, returning null like every destructor here.
- `call_<target>_ret_null_<addr>`: call `target`, return a null pointer (1037; most common targets `0x7e205040` ×608, `0x7e1e67f6` ×173, `0x7e2daa34` ×54, `0x7e33c67e` ×40, `0x7dfd5731` ×25, `0x7e34f411` ×24).
- `call_<target>_ret_ptr_<value>` / `call_<target>_ret_<value>`: call `target`, return a fixed address or number.
- `call_<target>_arg_<value>`: call `target` with `d0` set to a constant. `call_<target>_on_<address>`:
  call it on an object at a fixed address. `call_<target>_on_g<address>`: on the object whose pointer is
  stored at that address.
- `fwd_f<off>_to_<target>`: call `target` on the member object whose pointer is at `this+off`.
  `fwd_f<off>_vslot<n>`: call that member object's vtable slot `+n`.
- `adj_thunk_<n>_to_<target>`: add `n` to `this`, then call `target` (entry for a base or member sub-object).
  `this_plus_<n>`: return `this+n`.
- `call2_<a>_<b>`: call `a(this)`, then `b(this)`.
- `store_<value>_f<off>_call_<target>`: store a constant in a field, then call `target`.
  `store_<value>_f<a>_f<b>`: store the same constant in two fields.

## Register-save prologue entries (pattern family)
On this CPU a `call` instruction can save registers and reserve the stack frame itself, so the compiler
places a function's explicit prologue (`movm [regs],(sp)` and/or `add -N,sp`) *in front of* the address
that direct calls use. Ghidra lists that 3- to 7-byte prologue as a function of its own. Each row here is
such a prologue with a function starting right after it: the same routine, entered here when it is called
through a pointer or a vtable slot, and at the body address when called directly. 2969 listed, named
`prologue_of_<body address>_<address>`; 1630 of the bodies have a name, shown in the role column. The
references counted in the xrefs column (vtable slots, mostly) belong to the routine as a whole.

## Small call wrappers, second pass: constructors, type checks, store-then-call (pattern family)
Unlabelled functions of at most 24 bytes, classified from their disassembly on 2026-11-13 by
`tools/func_patterns.py small 24`. 2770 listed; 1689 rows end with `Target: <name>` because the call target
already has a name. Shapes that are new in this pass:
- `ctor_vt<vtable>_base_<target>[_f<off>_<value>]` (553): calls `target`, then stores a code-block address at
  offset 0 of the returned object, optionally followed by one constant field. This is how constructors look
  here: base constructor, then the class's own vtable pointer. In the bank around `0x7dfc2b00` the extra
  field is a 16-bit number at `+4` that differs by one from class to class, so it reads as a class id.
- `s16_eq_<id>_ret_<k>_else_<target>` (502) and `u16_eq_<id>_ret_<k>_else_<target>` (250): return a constant
  when the argument equals one number, otherwise pass the argument on to `target`. Next to the constructors
  above the number is the same class id, which makes these "is this object of class id N, or of a base
  class" checks; elsewhere the meaning of the number was not established.
- `store_<value>_f<a>_f<b>_call_<target>` (927): store one constant in two fields, then call `target`.
- `call_<target>_on_g<address>_arg_<value>[_ret0]`: call `target` on the object whose pointer is stored at a
  fixed address, with a constant argument. `call_<target>_and_<mask>`: return the target's result masked.
The remaining names follow the first pass above.

## Small call wrappers, third pass: framed thunks, constructors with arguments, call sequences (pattern family)
Unlabelled functions of at most 32 bytes, classified on 2026-11-13 by `tools/func_patterns.py small 32`.
1158 listed; 501 rows end with `Target: <name>`.
- `thunk_to_<target>` (398): `add -N,sp; call target; ret` — a plain thunk that reserves its own stack frame
  (the frameless form is listed under "One-instruction accessors, empty functions and thunks").
- `ctor_vt<vtable>_base_<target>_init` (550): the constructor shape of the second pass with constant arguments
  for the base constructor and/or more than one field initialised afterwards; the role column quotes both.
- `call3_<a>_<b>_<c>` (130): three calls in a row on `this`. `call0_<target>` (33): call, return 0.
  `ret_<value>` (47): return a constant.

## Byte-identical routine copies: pairs and copies of named functions (pattern family)
Second pass of the byte-identical scan (see "Byte-identical routine copies" above), 2026-11-13, now over
every function of 8 to 400 bytes and down to groups of two (unnamed groups in the first
64 kB of the code block, the start-up region, are left out). 498 listed in 243 groups.
- `<name>_copy_<address>` (32): the bytes equal those of a function that already has a name; the copy does
  the same thing with its own neighbours, so the name carries over.
- `copy<N>x_<first address>_<address>` (466): two or three identical copies, none named yet; the row lists
  the others and quotes the opening instructions.

the whole firmware, and that reference is a call from a function with a hand-analysed name (`symbol-map.md`) or one of the
firmware's own `Class::method` names; guessed and structural names do not count. Such a
function is a private helper of its caller, so it is named `<caller>_sub_<address>`. Helpers of helpers are
followed up to three levels. 1590 listed. The name places the function; it does not say what it does, and none
of these were read. Functions in the first 64 kB of the code block and callers whose names concern flash
